Together, they mark the next step on our scaling ladder and a major leap toward personal superintelligence. Muse Wonder brings together Active Memory and Active Focus to keep track of what matters to you and work diligently toward what you want to accomplish.

Muse Wonder is available today through the Meta Model API and Muse Code, and Muse Wonder Full is available today for Muse Code subscribers.

When we introduced Muse Spark, we outlined our approach to predictable, rigorous scaling. ...

...

Two models often have similar benchmark scores, yet one seems to handle a much wider range of unfamiliar tasks. That’s what complaints of “benchmaxxing” and praise for “big model smell” both get at: a breadth of capability that popular benchmarks in a few domains can’t fully capture.

To quantify this mismatch, we investigate how performance on tasks targeted during post-training relates to performance on unfamiliar tasks as we scale test-time compute. The plot below compares Muse Spark 1.3 and Muse Wonder Full, with each point denoting performance at a distinct reasoning effort. The horizontal axis shows the model’s score on a composite representative of the tasks we focused on during post-training (“in-distribution”). The vertical axis shows the average score on a set of tasks we did not target during post-training (“out-of-distribution”).

Both of our models improve similarly on out-of-distribution tasks as we scale test-time compute. But given its in-distribution performance, Muse Wonder Full performs even better on unfamiliar tasks than the Muse Spark 1.3 trend would predict. Muse Wonder offers our strongest safeguards to date against CBRN (chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear) and cyber misuse, while preserving access to frontier cyber capabilities for defensive use, per our Meta Superintelligence Scaling Framework.

signals.excerpt:
AI By Crimson AI Hugging Face Papers 12 October 2026 · 00:00 5 views 

A new Hugging Face paper introduces SoloQ, a calibration-free quantization framework for diffusion large language models that preserves accuracy at 4-bit precision and cuts peak memory by up to 2.61x.
...
- SoloQ is a calibration-free post-training quantization framework for diffusion large language models.
- It maps weights and activations into a normalized rotated basis with a predictable marginal distribution, using a structured K-RPBH rotation plus a lightweight rescaling correction.
- The approach supports both distribution-matched codebooks and hardware-native NVFP4.
- For block-diffusion models, commit-time KV-cache quantization compresses persistent states without perturbing the actively denoised block.
- SoloQ retains accuracy under 4-bit quantization and beats calibration-based baselines on knowledge- and reasoning-intensive benchmarks across LLaDA, Dream, Fast-dLLM v2, and Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion.
- With NVFP4, it reduces peak memory by up to 2.61x and accelerates end-to-end inference by up to 2.24x.
...
Enter SoloQ, a calibration-free quantization framework from researchers publishing on Hugging Face. SoloQ maps weights and activations into a normalized rotated basis with a predictable marginal distribution, enabling data-independent quantization. It combines a structured K-RPBH rotation with a lightweight rescaling correction, and its predictable post-rotation distribution supports both distribution-matched codebooks and hardware-native NVFP4.

For block-diffusion models, SoloQ adds commit-time KV-cache quantization, compressing persistent states without disturbing the block currently being denoised.

Across full-sequence dLLMs (LLaDA and Dream) and block-diffusion dLLMs (Fast-dLLM v2 and Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion), SoloQ retains accuracy under 4-bit quantization and outperforms calibration-based baselines on knowledge- and reasoning-intensive benchmarks. With NVFP4, it reduces peak memory by up to 2.61x and accelerates end-to-end inference by up to 2.24x.

| --- | --- |
| Quantization precision | 4-bit (retains accuracy) |
| Peak memory reduction (NVFP4) | Up to 2.61x |
| End-to-end inference speedup (NVFP4) | Up to 2.24x |
| Models evaluated | LLaDA, Dream, Fast-dLLM v2, Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion |

signals.excerpt:
Odin 0.4.0: Graph Retrieval with Explicit Backends | Prescott Data

# Odin 0.4.0: ... Retrieval with Explicit Backends

Explore Odin 0.4.0 knowledge graph retrieval: explicit ArangoDB backends, persistent learned models, convergence-driven training, and the API migration guide.
...
Odin 0.4.0 makes the boundary between a knowledge graph and its retrieval engine explicit. Applications supply a backend, map their own collections and relationship fields, and decide which optional metadata signals to enable. Learned scoring state now survives restarts as a complete, revision-checked model artifact. Training must converge before that artifact can replace a serving model. The release also repairs the JanusGraph accessor, expands training diagnostics, and packages separate skills for using Odin and implementing a backend.
...
Previously, an application could pass an Arango database handle directly to `OdinEngine`. That bound engine construction and learned-model management to one database implementation. The backend abstraction in PR #11 replaces that construction with a `GraphBackend` whose `accessor(community_id, community_mode)` supplies graph traversal. Training and persistence are separate capabilities: a `TripleSource` materializes a training snapshot, and a `ModelStore` loads and atomically saves complete artifacts.

These contracts live under the public `odin.backends` import path. A custom backend can implement traversal without implementing training. With automatic training enabled, missing source or store capabilities raise `BackendCapabilityError`. Choosing `auto_train=False` explicitly enables structural retrieval with constant confidence; it neither loads a cached learned model nor silently rescues a failed training request. Engine validation also rejects accessors that merely inherit unimplemented protocol methods.

`ArangoBackend` supplies the engine, training, persistence, and schema-inspection integration. Database drivers are optional dependencies: the core installation no longer requires `python-arango` or `gremlinpython`. Install the `arango` extra for ArangoDB or the `gremlin` extra for the JanusGraph accessor. This separation lets an in-memory or custom integration import Odin without installing unrelated database clients.

The JanusGraph repair is independently significant. Its previous accessor unpacked Gremlin result dictionaries as tuples, read edge properties with the wrong shape, and used a constructor API removed from modern gremlinpython. The rewritten accessor uses `project()` queries returning plain values, adds inbound traversal and node lookup, and supports a configurable weight property. PR #10 contains the accessor rewrite. It does not supply JanusGraph training or model persistence. Direct orchestrator integration or a caller-written backend is still required. Neo4j engine support and cross-database parity validation remain deferred.

# ReplaySSM: Rethinking State Storage for Faster Hybrid-Model Decoding | NVIDIA Technical Blog

Author: Michelle Horton
Published: 2026-10-12T16:00:54Z
Source: developer.nvidia.com
...
Building on earlier ReplaySSM work, NVIDIA and the Dao AI Lab at Princeton University explore how caching SSM inputs speeds up decoding and supports low-precision state with less error accumulation.
...
* ReplaySSM represents state-space model state as a checkpoint plus a buffer of recent inputs, separating output computation from state updates.
* The technique reduces state memory traffic by roughly half, speeding up SSM decoding kernels by 1.46x to 1.80x at batch size 256 on NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs.
* ReplaySSM simplifies speculative decoding rollback by appending draft inputs to a buffer instead of snapshotting state, delivering 1.85x to 2.10x higher speculative throughput on 120B-class models.
* Using a high-precision checkpoint for recurrence and a low-precision copy for reads limits quantization error accumulation, keeping three of four evaluated models within about 2 percentage points of FP32 accuracy on GPQA-Diamond.
...

ReplaySSM makes SSM layers the fast part again. It represents the SSM state as a checkpoint plus a buffer of recent inputs. This separates output computation from state updates and addresses three challenges in current SSM decoding: state traffic, rollback for speculative decoding, and error accumulation in a quantized state.
ReplaySSM is joint work between NVIDIA and the Dao AI Lab at Princeton. The paper, ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State, details all three benefits and presents the full evaluation. It is available on arXiv, with code on GitHub. It is integrated into NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, and FlashInfer, and also runs in production in GLM-5.3-Flash and Kimi-K3.
...
## How we evaluated ReplaySSM
We evaluate four hybrid models from two families, Nemotron 3 with Mamba-2 layers and Qwen3.5 with GDN layers, from 4B dense models on one NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPU to 120B-class mixture-of-experts (MoE) models on one NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra B300 GPU (Table 1). We implemented ReplaySSM in vLLM and compared it with vLLM’s own kernels at their best launch configuration.
Performance runs keep the SSM state in FP32, the default precision for these models, and use a window of *L* = 16, the best-performing window size for all four models. Speculative decoding tests use each model’s multi-token prediction (MTP) head to generate draft tokens.
|**Model**|**SSM layer**|**Weights**|**GPU**|**SSM / attention layers**|
|Nemotron-3-Nano-4B|Mamba-2|BF16|1×H100|21 / 4|
|Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B|Mamba-2|NVFP4|1×B300|40 / 8|
|Qwen3.5-4B|GDN|BF16|1×H100|24 / 8|

Table 1. ... *## Benefit 1: Reduce state memory traffic
Over a window of *L* tokens, conventional decoding reads the state *L* times and writes it *L* times. ReplaySSM still reads the checkpoint on every step, because the output needs it, but writes it only once, during the flush. A non-flush step has one job—computing the output—and writes only the new input record, a few vectors instead of a full matrix. This roughly halves the dominant state traffic.
At serving batch sizes, memory bandwidth limits the conventional kernel’s performance, so reducing state memory traffic speeds up decoding. At batch size 1, other sources of latency dominate, and ReplaySSM provides no speedup in these tests. At batch size 256, the kernel runs 1.46× to 1.80× faster, and the decode step runs 1.20× to 1.47× faster across the four models (Figure 3). The end-to-end gain grows with batch size because the SSM share of the step grows.

In speculative decoding, ReplaySSM appends the inputs of all *T* draft tokens to the input buffer before verification and commits the accepted prefix afterward by advancing the buffer pointer. A flush folds only committed records into the checkpoint, so it never waits for the accepted length.

ReplaySSM writes no state on most steps, so it verifies eight tokens in about the time of one standard step, flushes included (Figure 5).

A developer has demonstrated the feasibility of running high-context, large language model (LLM) inference on consumer-grade hardware using advanced quantization techniques, according to a discussion on Reddit. The findings highlight the performance advantages of NVFP4 quantization compared to standard FP8 formats when operating within the memory constraints of high-end consumer GPUs like the NVIDIA RTX 5090.

While the standard Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 model carries a repository size of approximately 30.9GB as noted on Hugging Face, which poses significant challenges for maintaining large context windows on 32GB VRAM cards, the NVFP4 implementation offers a more efficient alternative. This allows for significantly higher context lengths and improved throughput by reducing the memory footprint without substantial loss in reasoning accuracy.

The positioning is explicit: ML4 is intended as an autonomous coding engine capable of executing terminal commands, calling external tools, and enforcing structured outputs, not just a conversational chatbot.

Mistral also addressed enterprise adoption friction. Behind the "Le Chonk" branding, the company published rigorous downstream-provider technical documentation—provider identification, publication dates, and general-purpose AI classification status—before weights were released. # SGL ... NVIDIA Vera Rubin
...
We had early access to two NVIDIA Vera Rubin nodes (8 GPUs) and used them to bring SGLang and Miles up on the platform: SGLang for inference and Miles for RL training. On the inference side, we tuned SGLang for Kimi K3 NVFP4: this post covers what we changed in the attention, MoE/communication and KDA kernels, and how much each change bought. On the training side, Miles, which uses SGLang for rollout and Megatron for training, runs RL end to end on Vera Rubin out of the box, including agentic RL with sandboxes on the Vera CPU.

NVIDIA Vera Rubin is the GPU generation after NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra (GB300 NVL72). For kernel work, the most impactful changes are more shared memory per CTA (327 KiB, up from the 227 KiB on NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell), more SMs (212 on our nodes), and NVIDIA NVLink 6. Some of our changes retune Blackwell-era kernels for these new limits. The rest remove overheads we found while profiling Kimi K3 on Rubin, such as kernel launches, barrier stalls and hidden copies.

Cognition has deployed Vera Rubin NVL72 with its own SGLang-based stack and has reported up to a 4.8x increase in total token throughput over GB200 NVL72. 1

## Inference:
...
Kimi K3 is a 2.8T-parameter hybrid model with a 1M-token context window. Its 93 attention layers interleave 69 KDA linear-attention layers with 24 MLA layers, and every attention output is banked and aggregated per block through Attention Residuals. The FFN is a LatentMoE with 896 experts, top-16 routing, running in a 3584-dimensional latent space. We serve the NVFP4 checkpoint with RadixArk's DSpark block speculative decoding, so every decode step is a short draft pass followed by a verify pass over the drafted tokens.
...
MLA pipelines. ... long context settings, MLA decode spends most of its time waiting on KV reads from HBM, and ... hide that is to keep more reads in flight. On Blackwell ... the FP8 kernel had already filled its ... 7 KiB of shared memory with 3 K stages and 2 V stages. Vera Rubin raises the per-CTA limit to 3 ... 7 KiB, just enough for a fourth K stage and two more V stages. With the deeper pipeline, MLA at batch 16 and 1 ... 8k context runs 16 ... faster, with bit-identical output.
...
FP8 conversion
...
Fused MoE tail. Every MoE layer ends the same way: finalize the expert outputs, add the shared expert, all-reduce across 8 GPUs, then RMSNorm. Each of those kernels is tiny, so launch overhead dominates, and K3 pays it in all 92 MoE layers. We defer the finalization and fold all four steps into one collective kernel. That removes 276 launches per decode step and gives 5.9% end to end.
...
The fused tail ... all-reduce for small batches
...
Less stall in KDA verify. KDA's fused verify kernel spent much of its time waiting at barriers instead of computing. Every CTA copied its conv weights into shared memory and then waited at a block-wide barrier. Now each warp keeps its own weights in registers. State handoffs that stay inside one warp require no CTA barriers. The v warps finish precomputing early, so they now use that idle time to compute the output-norm gate. Outputs stay bitwise identical. On Vera Rubin, the production verify kernel sped up by 20%.
...
Strided output gate. The gated RMSNorm in each KDA ... takes its gate from a column slice of the fused QKVG projection. Because the slice isn ... t contiguous, PyTorch silently copied it before every call: 2.6 µs, 69 times per step. Teaching the norm kernel to read the gate through its strides removed the copy ... cut decode step time
...

Miles runs RL training end to end on NVIDIA Vera Rubin, with SGLang for rollout and Megatron for training, from a single container image. With the Rubin-enablement PR in place, these RL runs were launched out of the box using Miles, on a single tray (4 GPUs):

- Qwen3-30B-A3B on GSM8K (256 prompts × 8 samples per ... , up to 1,024 response tokens): training converges as expected, ... reward rising from ... 45% to 95% over 5 ... rollouts ( ... reward growth curve perfectly.
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash (4-layer ... on GSM8K (32 prompts × 8 samples per step, up to 256 response tokens): the FP8 path runs end-to-end for both rollout and training.
...
These are promising initial results demonstrating Miles' readiness on Vera Rubin. The next phase will focus on scaling up and further improving performance.
...
As a first step toward agentic RL on Vera Rubin, we run it on a single tray with NeMo Gym's mini-SWE-agent environment: each episode gets its own sandbox on the tray's Vera CPU, next to the GPUs that serve and train Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, with 64 sandboxes running at once. We chose SWE-bench Verified because it ships prebuilt arm64 task images, and we verified that grading works on them. Each step samples 8 tasks × 8 attempts from a 64-task pool, with up to 64K tokens per episode. Training runs normally with all environments on the Arm-based Vera CPU: the reward holds at about 0.6, episodes get about 30% shorter, and rollout and training stay closely matched (Figure 4). Once Vera CPU servers are available at scale, we look forward to agentic training with far more concurrent environments.
...

On inference, we'll keep rolling out optimizations to take full advantage of the platform across a wider range of production workloads. 【收藏版】LLM+MCP融合RAG与Agent：用TaoToken统一Key打通「知行合一」的大模型智能系统-港品优选
...
LLM 负责理解与生成，MCP 负责把工具调用标准化，RAG 负责把外部知识喂进来，Agent 负责把多步任务串起来。这四个东西单独用都能跑，但拼在一起才是「知行合一」——既懂知识，又会动手。问题在于，很多人在拼接阶段就卡死了：模型 Key 散落在四五个平台，OpenAI 一个、Claude 一个、国产模型又一个，每个 SDK 的鉴权方式还不一样，config.toml 和 settings.json 改到崩溃。

这篇就是来解决这个问题的。我会用 TaoToken 作为统一 Key 与 API 通道，把多模型调用收敛到一个入口，然后给你可复制的 config.toml、settings.json 骨架，再走一遍 CC Switch / Cline 接入、RAG 检索验证、Agent 工具调用的完整链路。适合已经写过一点 LangChain 或 LlamaIndex、但被多 Key 管理搞烦的开发者。全程可跟做，代码能直接抄。
...
在动手写 RAG 和 Agent 之前，先把「模型从哪来」这件事解决掉。传统做法是每个模型平台注册一个账号、拿一个 Key、写一套鉴权代码，项目里到处是`OPENAI_API_KEY`、`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`、`DASHSCOPE_API_KEY`，换模型等于改代码。TaoToken 的思路是提供一个统一的 API 通道，你用同一个 Key 就能调用不同厂商的模型，base_url 指向同一个地址，SDK 层面几乎不用改。

具体操作分三步。第一步，打开官网 https://taotoken.net/?utm_source=taotoken_aicg_blog_end&utm_medium=csdn&utm_campaign=rewrite&utm_content= 注册账号。第二步，进入控制台 https://taotoken.net/console?utm_source=taotoken_aicg_blog_end&utm_campaign=rewrite&utm_content= 创建 API Key，建议按项目分 Key，方便后面做权限隔离和用量追踪。第三步，记下 API 地址 https://taotoken.net/api，这个地址就是你所有 SDK 里的 base_url。
...
如果返回正常的 JSON 结构，说明通道没问题。这一步很关键，因为后面 RAG 的 embedding、Agent 的规划调用，全都依赖这个通道。通道不通，后面全是玄学报错。
...
```
# config.toml [api] base_url = "https://taotoken.net/api/v1" api_key = "sk-你的TaoToken密钥" timeout = 60 max_retries = 3 [models] # 主力对话模型，用于 Agent 任务规划 planner = "gpt-4o-mini" # 知识问答模型，用于 RAG 结果生成 rag_llm = "gpt-4o-mini" # 向量化模型，用于文档索引 embedding = "text-embedding-3-small" # 备用模型，主模型超时或限流时切换 fallback = "claude-3-5-sonnet" [rag] chunk_size = 1024 chunk_overlap = 200 top_k = 5 index_dir = "./storage/indices" [agent] max_steps = 8 tool_timeout = 30 enable_review = true
...
这里的关键是`[api]`段：所有模型共用同一个 base_url 和 api_key，切换模型只改`[models]`里的字符串。`fallback`字段是给生产环境用的，主模型限流时自动降级，避免整个 Agent 卡死。
...
```
{ "llm": { "provider": "openai-compatible", "baseUrl": "https://taotoken.net/api/v1", "apiKey": "sk-你的TaoToken密钥", "model": "gpt-4o-mini", "temperature": 0.1, "maxTokens": 4096 }, "mcp": { "servers": { "rag-server": { "command": "python", "args": ["mcp_rag_server.py", "--port", "8000"], "env": { "TAOTOKEN_API_KEY": "sk-你的TaoToken密钥", "TAOTOKEN_BASE_URL": "https://taotoken.net/api/v1" } } } }, "rag": { "indexName": "default-index", "topK": 5, "similarityThreshold": 0.7 } }
...
`provider`填`openai-compatible`是因为 TaoToken 的接口兼容 OpenAI 协议，绝大多数客户端都能直接识别。`mcp.servers`段是给 MCP 服务端用的，把 RAG 服务注册成一个 MCP Server，Agent 就能通过标准协议发现并调用它。
...
### 4. 验证请求：RAG 检索与 Agent 调用跑通

配置写好了，接下来验证两件事：RAG 能不能检索到知识，Agent 能不能调用工具。这两步跑通，整条链路就活了。
...
先写一个最小的 RAG 检索脚本，用 TaoToken 的 embedding 通道建索引：

```
# rag_verify.py import os from llama_index.core import VectorStoreIndex, SimpleDirectoryReader, Settings from llama_index.embeddings.openai import OpenAIEmbedding from llama_index.llms.openai import OpenAI # 统一指向 TaoToken 通道 Settings.embed_model = OpenAIEmbedding( model="text-embedding-3-small", api_key=os.getenv("TAOTOKEN_API_KEY"), api_base="https://taotoken.net/api/v1" ) Settings.llm = OpenAI( model="gpt-4o-mini", api_key=os.getenv("TAOTOKEN_API_KEY"), api_base="https://taotoken.net/api/v1" ) # 加载文档并建索引 documents = SimpleDirectoryReader("./docs").load_data() index = VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(documents) # 检索验证 query_engine = index.as_query_engine(similarity_top_k=5) response = query_engine.query("文档里提到的核心结论是什么？") print(response)
...
#### 4.2 Agent 工具调用验证

Agent 的核心是「规划 → 调用 → 评审」循环。下面是一个最小可跑的 ReAct Agent，通过 MCP 协议调用 RAG 工具：

```
# agent_verify.py import asyncio from langgraph.graph import Graph, END from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI from langchain.schema import HumanMessage, SystemMessage llm = ChatOpenAI( model="gpt-4o-mini", api_key=os.getenv("TAOTOKEN_API_KEY"), base_url="https://taotoken.net/api/v1", temperature=0.1 ) def plan_node(state): prompt = f"""你是任务规划专家。用户需求：{state['query']} 可用工具：query_document(index_name, query, top_k) 请输出执行步骤，每步一行，格式：步骤N：调用工具名，参数：{{...}}""" resp = llm.invoke([SystemMessage(content=prompt)]) state["plan"] = resp.content return state def execute_node(state): # 这里对接你的 MCP 工具执行器 # 实际项目中通过 MCPClient 调用 rag-server state["result"] = "工具执行完成" return state workflow = Graph() workflow.add_node("planner", plan_node) workflow.add_node("executor", execute_node) workflow.add_edge("planner", "executor") workflow.add_edge("executor", END) workflow.set_entry_point("planner") app = workflow.compile() result = asyncio.run(app.ainvoke({"query": "对比北京和上海的小微企业政策"})) print(result["plan"]) print(result["result"])
...
跑通后你会看到 Agent 自动生成了执行计划，并调用了 RAG 工具。这就是「知行合一」的最小闭环：LLM 规划、MCP 调度、RAG 供知识、Agent 执行。
...
Agent 报`no tools available`，一般是 MCP Server 没启动或 settings.json 里的`mcp.servers`配置不对。先手动跑`python mcp_rag_server.py --port 8000`，确认服务端能起来，再检查客户端配置里的 command 和 args 是否匹配。端口被占用也是常见原因，换 8001 试试。
...
Agent 反复规划同一个步骤，通常是评审节点没生效。检查`enable_review`是否为 true，以及评审 prompt 是否明确要求输出「满足」或「不满足」。如果评审结果解析失败，Agent 会默认继续，导致循环。加一个`max_steps`上限兜底，超过就强制结束。
...
taotoken
...
第二，如果你要做长期编码或 Agent 项目，建议用 Coding Plan https://taotoken.net/coding-plan?utm_source=taotoken_aicg_blog_end&utm_campaign=rewrite&utm_content= 管理用量和额度，避免项目跑到一半 Key 限流。ClaudeCodeAnthropic 接入也可以走同一个通道，配置方式类似，把 base_url 换成 TaoToken 地址即可。

第三，把 RAG 的索引管理和 Agent 的工具注册做成可配置的，新增业务工具时只改 settings.json，不动核心代码。这样你的系统就能从「能跑」进化到「好维护」。

最后留一个实用技巧：每次改完配置，先用 curl 验证通道，再跑 RAG 检索，最后跑 Agent 全链路。分层验证能帮你快速定位问题出在哪一层，比一上来就跑全链路然后对着报错发呆高效得多。

signals.title: Saluki 27B: 7.89 GB Quantized Qwen3 Beats Original at Tool Calling — AI In Context
signals.excerpt:
Saluki 27B: 7.89 GB Quantized Qwen3 Beats Original at Tool Calling — AI In Context

# Saluki 27B: A 7.89 GB, 2-Bit Qwen3.8 That Beats the 54 GB Original at Tool Calling

Underdog's Saluki 27B compresses Qwen3.8-27B to 7.89 GB in 2-bit GGUF and beats the 54 GB original at tool calling: 88 vs 84 on its 120-task BFCL v4 benchmark.
...
- Saluki 27B is a 2-bit GGUF of Qwen3.8-27B that fits in 7.89 GB, versus 54 GB for the full BF16 model.
- It beats the original at tool calling: 88 vs 84 on Underdog's 120-task BFCL v4 benchmark, and 42 vs 35 on parallel tool calls.
- It runs in stock llama.cpp under Apache 2.0, with optional 629 MB or 928 MB vision add-ons.
- Math takes the biggest hit: AIME 2025 drops from 96.7 to 79.2 (about 82% retention).
- Average retention is 96% across 9 benchmarks versus the full model, according to Underdog.

Underdog has squeezed Qwen3.8-27B into a 7.89 GB file that beats the original 54 GB model at tool calling. The release, called Underdog Saluki 27B, is a 2-bit, mixed-precision GGUF published under Apache 2.0 by Conway Research, the company behind the Underdog on-device assistant. On Underdog's 120-task tool-calling benchmark built from BFCL v4, Saluki scores 88 while the full BF16 model scores 84.

The numbers matter because tool calling is the skill that turns a chat model into an agent. Developers get a 27B-class agent model that runs in stock llama.cpp, with full GPU offload, on hardware that could never hold the 54 GB original.
...
- The quantization layer: ISTA-DASLab's Qwen3.8-27B-GSQ-RCO-GGUF. GSQ learns accurate low-bit scalar grids per tensor; RCO assigns a quantization type to each tensor under a fixed size budget. ISTA's smallest file, IQ2_XS, is 8.4 GB at 2.50 bits per weight.
- Underdog's own pass: the company shrank the file further to 7.89 GB and tuned the compression to protect tool calling. The file is named `IQ2-mix` and carries an imatrix tag. Underdog has not published the full recipe.

That final, undisclosed pass is what separates Saluki from a standard quantization release — and it's where the tool-calling gains come from.
...
| Feature | Saluki 27B | Qwen3.8-27B (BF16) | ISTA GSQ-RCO IQ2_XS | PrismML Bonsai 2 (PTQ1_0) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Org | Underdog (Conway Research) | Qwen team | ISTA-DASLab | PrismML |
| Parameters | 27B | 27B | 27B | 27.36B |
| File size | 7.89 GB | 54 GB | 8.4 GB | 5.95 GB |
| Bits per weight | Not disclosed (2-bit mix) | 16 | 2.50 | 1.75 |
| Context | Not disclosed | 262,144 native | Not disclosed | 262K |
| Vision | Add-on, 629 or 928 MB | Native | 0.9 GB mmproj | Optional 0.63 GB |
| Runtime | Stock llama.cpp | Transformers, vLLM, SGLang | Stock llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio | PrismML llama.cpp fork |
| Underdog Bench (of 120) | 88 | 84 | Not disclosed | 70 |
| License | Apache 2.0 | Apache 2.0 | Apache 2.0 | Apache 2.0 |

Bonsai 2 is smaller and reports ... 8.2% retention across 14 thinking- ... stronger math — 95. ... . But it ... PrismML's llama.cpp fork, since stock llama.cpp rejects its packing
...
The local-agent market is the stakes here. A 27B model at 7.89 GB fits on consumer hardware — laptops, single-GPU boxes — and still handles the tool-calling loop that agent frameworks depend on. Saluki's pitch is that compression doesn't have to be uniform: you can spend your precision budget where the workload lives, and accept losses in math you'll never run.

Underdog hasn't disclosed the exact bits-per-weight or context window for the file, and the tuning recipe is unpublished. For now, the model card on Hugging Face, the Underdog launch page, and the announcement on X carry everything the company has shared. If the undisclosed recipe holds up under independent testing, expect targeted quantization to become a standard move for anyone shipping local agent models.
